question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of ultrasound imaging over computed tomography (CT) scans?

options.A: It utilizes high doses of ionizing radiation.
options.B: It is completely free of radiation hazards.
options.C: It is strictly invasive and requires general anesthesia.
options.D: It only provides static, non-real-time images.

explanation: Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves rather than ionizing radiation, making it safe for repeated use without radiation risks. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is it important for medical-surgical nurses to understand the fundamentals of ultrasound?

options.A: To perform independent radiologic interpretations without a physician.
options.B: To replace the need for all laboratory diagnostic tests.
options.C: To provide patient education, ensure proper positioning, and assist with procedures.
options.D: To calibrate and repair the electronic ultrasound equipment.

explanation: Nurses need foundational knowledge to educate patients, assist effectively during procedures, and ensure proper patient positioning and care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying acoustic gel to the patient's skin prior to an ultrasound examination?

options.A: To cool down the transducer and prevent patient burns.
options.B: To eliminate air pockets and facilitate sound wave transmission.
options.C: To act as a strong antiseptic against skin pathogens.
options.D: To permanently stain tissues for better contrast enhancement.

explanation: Air poorly conducts ultrasound waves; acoustic gel removes air pockets between the probe and skin to allow smooth sound wave transmission. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h2)

question: How do fluid-filled structures typically appear on a standard ultrasound monitor?
explanation: Fluid-filled structures allow sound waves to pass through with little reflection, appearing dark or black (anechoic) on the screen. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which type of ultrasound probe is best suited for superficial structures and vascular access due to its high near-field resolution?
explanation: High-frequency linear probes provide high-resolution images of superficial structures and are ideal for vascular access and shallow tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical utility of Doppler ultrasound in medical-surgical nursing?

options.A: Evaluating blood flow velocity and direction in vessels
options.B: Measuring bone density and detecting micro-fractures
options.C: Delivering therapeutic heat to deep muscle spasms
options.D: Generating static 3D photographs of internal organs

explanation: Doppler ultrasound evaluates blood flow dynamics and direction by measuring frequency shifts caused by moving red blood cells. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h3)

question: What does the FAST exam primarily evaluate in trauma patients?

options.B: Free fluid in peritoneal, pericardial, and pleural spaces
options.C: Coronary artery blockages and myocardial infarction
options.D: Bone fractures in the upper and lower extremities

explanation: The FAST exam is a rapid bedside ultrasound protocol used in trauma to detect free fluid in key body cavities. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h4)

question: How does ultrasound improve safety during invasive procedures like thoracentesis or central line insertion?

options.A: By completely eliminating the need for local anesthesia
options.B: By real-time visualization, reducing complications like accidental puncture
options.C: By chemically sterilizing the insertion site before entry
options.D: By automatically suturing the wound after catheter removal

explanation: Real-time ultrasound guidance allows clinicians to visualize needle paths and internal structures, greatly lowering complication rates. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is a patient scheduled for an abdominal ultrasound usually instructed to remain NPO (fasting) for 6 to 8 hours prior?

options.A: To prevent aspiration pneumonia during the procedure
options.B: To minimize bowel gas and ensure the gallbladder is distended
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions to the water-soluble gel

explanation: Fasting reduces gas in the gastrointestinal tract and allows the gallbladder to fill with bile, making it easier to visualize. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for instructing a patient to have a full bladder before a pelvic or renal ultrasound?

options.A: To stimulate peristalsis and bowel evacuation
options.B: To act as an acoustic window and push bowel loops out of the pelvis
options.C: To test the patient's renal concentrating ability
options.D: To prevent urinary tract infections during probe insertion

explanation: A full bladder serves as an acoustic window that displaces gas-filled bowel loops and enhances visualization of pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which of the following is a key intra-procedural nursing responsibility during a sterile ultrasound-guided procedure like a paracentesis?

options.A: Operating the ultrasound machine console independently
options.B: Maintaining strict aseptic technique and monitoring vital signs
options.C: Administering general anesthesia to keep the patient motionless
options.D: Disposing of all reusable metal transducers in sharps containers

explanation: Nurses must maintain sterility, set up equipment, and continuously monitor the patient's hemodynamic status during invasive procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h6)

question: How should ultrasound transducers used for procedures involving sterile body cavities or non-intact skin be managed for infection control?

options.A: Wiped with a dry paper towel between patients
options.B: Washed with ordinary hand soap and tap water
options.C: Subjected to high-level disinfection (HLD) and sterile covers
options.D: Soaked in boiling water for five minutes

explanation: Probes entering sterile body cavities require sterile sheaths/covers and rigorous high-level disinfection to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h6)

question: What is an immediate post-procedure nursing action for a patient who has just completed an abdominal ultrasound?

options.A: Administering a dose of intravenous contrast dye
options.B: Cleaning leftover acoustic gel from the patient's skin and clothing
options.C: Initiating strict bedrest for the next 24 hours
options.D: Placing a pressure dressing over the entire abdomen

explanation: Wiping away residual acoustic gel ensures patient comfort and hygiene after the scan is completed. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h7)

question: What should a nurse do when reviewing an official ultrasound report that contradicts the patient's stable clinical assessment?

options.A: Ignore the report because clinical assessments are always more accurate.
options.B: Promptly communicate the discrepancy to the interprofessional healthcare team.
options.C: Repeat the entire ultrasound scan independently at the bedside.
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they appear clinically stable.

explanation: Nurses must correlate imaging reports with clinical findings and communicate any discrepancies to the medical team to ensure safe patient care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h7)

question: How does Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) primarily differ from comprehensive diagnostic sonography in radiology?

options.A: POCUS is performed at the bedside to answer specific, binary clinical questions.
options.B: POCUS utilizes high-dose radiation instead of sound waves.
options.C: POCUS can only be operated by certified radiologists.
options.D: POCUS takes several hours to generate real-time images.

explanation: POCUS is a bedside tool used by clinicians to quickly answer targeted clinical questions rather than performing a comprehensive radiology survey. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h8)

question: What is an important consideration for nurses utilizing POCUS in acute care settings?

options.A: It completely replaces all laboratory and physical assessments.
options.B: It requires proper competency training and adherence to scope-of-practice guidelines.
options.C: It should only be performed on discharged outpatients.
options.D: It eliminates the need for documenting findings in the patient chart.

explanation: Clinicians must undergo proper competency training and operate within their professional scope of practice when performing POCUS. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h8)
